title: Reindexing homotopy colimits along diagramwise weak-equivalence zigzags
statement: Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence, cofibrant-object and Reedy terminology of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A model category is combinatorial when its underlying category is locally presentable and its two weak factorization systems have small generating sets. An object is $\lambda$-presentable if its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits; $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone. Locally $\lambda$-presentable means generated under these colimits by a small family of $\lambda$-presentable objects. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial. For a small category $I$ and a diagram $V:I\to\mathcal M$, define $\operatorname{hocolim}_I V$ as $\operatorname{colim}_I Q_I V$, where $Q_I V\to V$ is a functorial cofibrant replacement for the projective diagram model structure (objectwise fibrations and weak equivalences), whose existence is part of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. These constructions preserve objectwise weak equivalences. Reindexing along $g:J\to I$ gives the canonical comparison $g_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_J(Vg)\to\operatorname{hocolim}_I V$ in the homotopy category, the ordinary localization at weak equivalences. Comparisons compose, and for a natural transformation $a:g\to g'$ the reindexing triangle commutes in the homotopy category with the map induced by $V(a)$. Suppose $I,J$ are small, $f:I\to J$, and there are finite zigzags of natural transformations connecting $gf$ to $\mathrm{id}_I$ and $fg$ to $\mathrm{id}_J$. Suppose every component of the first zigzag becomes a weak equivalence after applying $V$, and every component of the second becomes a weak equivalence after applying $Vg$. Then $g_*$ is an isomorphism in the homotopy category; any actual comparison map representing it is a weak equivalence. This includes natural isomorphisms and strict identities as special cases.

source.place: Remark A.3(i)-(iv), Proposition A.4 and Remark A.5, printed pp. 197-199. The zigzag version requires weak equivalences after applying the respective value diagrams, not just contractibility of the indexing nerves. No Stacks tag states this model-homotopy-colimit result. Sources read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] to the given combinatorial model category and each small indexing category. It supplies the projective structures and the coherent localization $q:N\mathcal M\to\mathcal C$. Put $H_I(V)=\operatorname{colim}_I Q_IV$. The cited statement makes the ordinary colimit cocone, after applying $q$ and inverting $q(Q_IV\to V)$, a coherent colimit cocone $\lambda_V:qV\to\operatorname{const}(qH_I(V))$. No simplicial-model-category hypothesis or objectwise cofibrancy of $V$ is required.

source.place: Remark A.3, choice of homotopy-colimit model; projective/coherent comparison via the cited existing node. The explicit ordinary-localization passage is an agent-supplied expansion.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] for this particular $q$, with $C=\mathcal M$ and $W$ its weak equivalences. The weak equivalences contain all identities and are closed under composition by two-out-of-three, so form the required wide subcategory. The full coherent localization property needed there is exactly the property supplied in Step 1. Enlarge universes as in both cited statements. It follows that $\gamma=hq:\mathcal M\to h\mathcal C$ has the ordinary localization universal property for functors and natural transformations. The same cited statement says that equivalence edges in $\mathcal C$ become isomorphisms in $h\mathcal C$. This supplies both functor and natural-transformation parts of the ordinary localization property.

source.place: Theorem 1.6.6, Corollary 1.6.8 and Remark 7.1.6, printed pp.24-25 and 325; ordinary-localization conclusion supplied by the existing cited node.

proof.text: Compare $\gamma$ with a strict ordinary localization $L:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$, initial on the nose among $W$-inverting functors. Its defining property gives $\Phi$ with $\Phi L=\gamma$. Apply the functor and natural-transformation universal property from Step 2, in the form stated in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], to obtain $\Psi:h\mathcal C\to\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$ and $\Psi\gamma\cong L$. Both $L$ and $\gamma$ have fully faithful restriction on functor categories by that cited statement. Hence the isomorphisms $\Psi\Phi L\cong L$ and $\Phi\Psi\gamma\cong\gamma$ lift uniquely to $\Psi\Phi\cong1$ and $\Phi\Psi\cong1$; the lifted transformations are isomorphisms because their inverses lift too and faithfulness verifies the inverse equations. Thus $\Phi$ is an equivalence and $\gamma(u)$ is invertible exactly when $L(u)$ is. We compute in $h\mathcal C$ and use this comparison whenever model saturation requires the strict localization.

source.place: Remark 7.1.6, printed p.325; uniqueness of ordinary localizations, using the full functor/natural-transformation universal property of the two cited statements.

proof.text: For a natural transformation $t:V\to V'$ on $I$, define $H_I(t)=\operatorname{colim}_I Q_I(t)$. Functoriality of $Q_I$ and of ordinary colimit gives identities and composition. Naturality of the replacement augmentation implies that $qH_I(t)$ carries $\lambda_V$ to $\lambda_{V'}\circ qt$; thus this actual map is the map of the localized colimits, by [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. If $t$ is objectwise a weak equivalence, $qt$ is a coherent equivalence by the componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Its coherent inverse gives the inverse map of colimits: apply the dual cocone mapping-space criterion there to the cocone $\lambda_V\circ(qt)^{-1}$, then compose with $qH_I(t)$. Both composites induce the original cocones, so the same criterion identifies them with the identities. Hence $\gamma H_I(t)$ is an isomorphism. The model-category saturation statement [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] makes the actual map $H_I(t)$ a weak equivalence. This proves the asserted homotopy invariance without requiring $V$ itself to be cofibrant.

source.place: Remark A.3(i); expanded for projective replacement using localized colimit cocones and model saturation.

proof.text: For any $g:J\to I$, restrict $\lambda_V$ to $N(J)$. This is a cocone on $q(Vg)$ with apex $qH_I(V)$. By the cocone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], its space of lifts along the colimit cocone $\lambda_{Vg}$ is contractible. Thus it determines a unique homotopy class $g_*^V:H_J(Vg)\to H_I(V)$. Here [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] supplies both colimit cocones with their actual structural maps. For $k:K\to J$, restricting first along $g$ and then $k$ gives exactly the same cocone as restriction along $gk$; uniqueness gives $(gk)_*^V=g_*^V\circ k_*^{Vg}$, and restriction along the identity gives the identity comparison. For a map $t:V\to V'$, both $H_I(t)\circ g_*^V$ and $g_*^{V'}\circ H_J(tg)$ induce the cocone $\lambda_{V'}\circ qt$ restricted along $g$, so they too agree in the homotopy category. These equalities use the full coherent cocones, not merely equality on their vertex components.

source.place: Remark A.3(ii)-(iii); construction and composition of reindexing comparisons from their cocones.

proof.text:
Let $a:g\Rightarrow g'$ be a natural transformation of functors $J\to I$. On $J\times[1]$ the corresponding functor sends $(j,0)$ to $g(j)$, $(j,1)$ to $g'(j)$, and a mixed arrow $(j,0)\to(j',1)$ to $g'(j\to j')a_j=a_{j'}g(j\to j')$. Naturality is precisely the equality needed for this to be a functor. Its nerve gives the coherent transformation $qV(a):qVg\to qVg'$ in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The naturality data of the cocone $\lambda_V$ on this prism identify the two cocones $\lambda_V|_g$ and $(\lambda_V|_{g'})\circ qV(a)$. Apply the cocone mapping-space criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] to $q(Vg)$: these cocone homotopies identify their lift classes. Consequently
$$g_*^V=(g')_*^V\circ H_J(V(a))$$
in $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)$. If $V(a)$ is objectwise a weak equivalence, Step 4 makes its $H_J$-map invertible, so $g_*^V$ is invertible if and only if $(g')_*^V$ is invertible. This assertion works in either orientation of a zigzag link.

source.place: Remark A.3(iv), with the natural-transformation prism and its effect on the cocones made explicit.

proof.text: Write the first stipulated finite zigzag as endofunctors $h_0=gf,h_1,\ldots,h_r=\mathrm{id}_I$, with either orientation allowed for each adjacent transformation. Step 6, applied to $V$, shows successively that $(h_i)_*^V$ is invertible if and only if $(h_{i+1})_*^V$ is. The endpoint identity comparison is invertible by Step 5; backwards induction therefore makes $(gf)_*^V$ invertible. Write the second zigzag as $k_0=fg,k_1,\ldots,k_s=\mathrm{id}_J$. For each link $k_i\Rightarrow k_{i+1}$, Step 6 for the value diagram $Vg$ gives $(k_i)_*^{Vg}=(k_{i+1})_*^{Vg}\circ H_J(Vg(a))$; the last factor is invertible by the second component hypothesis and Step 4. For a reverse link the displayed equality has its two comparison terms exchanged, which gives the identical invertibility equivalence. Starting with $(k_s)_*^{Vg}=1$ and inducting backwards proves $(fg)_*^{Vg}$ invertible. A zero-link zigzag is just the identity case; no compatibility between the two chosen zigzags has been assumed or used.

source.place: Remark A.5; finite backward induction expands the omitted zigzag argument.

proof.text:
Keep the two occurrences of the $g$ comparison distinct. Put
$$A=H_J(Vgfg),\quad B=H_I(Vgf),\quad C=H_J(Vg),\quad D=H_I(V),$$
and let $u=g_*^{Vgf}:A\to B$, $v=f_*^{Vg}:B\to C$, and $w=g_*^V:C\to D$. The composition formula of Step 5 identifies $vu=(fg)_*^{Vg}$ and $wv=(gf)_*^V$, so Step 7 makes both composites invertible. Then $l=(wv)^{-1}w:C\to B$ is a left inverse of $v$, and $r=u(vu)^{-1}:C\to B$ is a right inverse. They agree since $l=l(vr)=(lv)r=r$. Hence $v$ is invertible, and $w=(wv)v^{-1}$ is invertible as well. This is the required isomorphism $g_*^V$. The argument does not identify $g_*^{Vgf}$ with $g_*^V$.

source.place: Proposition A.4, proof, printed p.200; explicit inverse calculation for the two adjacent composites.

proof.text: If an actual model-category comparison map represents $g_*^V$, its image under $\gamma$ of Step 3 is the isomorphism of Step 8, so by the comparison $\Phi$ of Step 3 its image under the strict localization $L$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] to $L$, with no cofibrancy or fibrancy condition on its endpoints, to conclude that this map is a weak equivalence. Natural isomorphisms of indexing functors satisfy the component hypotheses because their images under any value functor are isomorphisms and every localization sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms; the same saturation statement then makes these images weak equivalences. Strict identities give zero-link zigzags and the identity comparisons of Step 5.

source.place: Proposition A.4, final sentence and Remark A.5; saturation as Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(iv).
